title: Structure every acceptance as Given/When/Then

facts.note: Acceptance definition files authored by the planner (legacy home: planner acceptance convention, section gherkin_structure).
Fires whenever an acceptance file is written or modified, regardless of which section changed.
Planning task that authors or revises one or more acceptances.

fires: Planner revises any part of an existing acceptance, even a single section (only given, only when, or only then)
Planner adds or changes an assertion in an acceptance's then
doesNotFire: Editing only a wagon or plan narrative that contains no acceptance
Coder implementing production code that an acceptance already describes
Editing docs that merely mention acceptances without defining one

given: You are authoring or revising an acceptance.
when: You write a new acceptance or change any of its sections (given, when or then — one is enough).
then: Give the acceptance a required `when` declaring the single harness-specific trigger and a required `then` that is an array of assertions, with `given` declaring only the required preconditions.
prefer: Express required preconditions in `given` using the listed precondition fields — auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs — and include a precondition only when the scenario needs it.
Shape `when` by harness: http → method/path; unit → target; event → topic; ws/e2e → interactions.
Use only allowed assertion kinds in `then`: status, body, headers, error, event_published, state_changed, metric.
avoid: More than one trigger in `when`, or a trigger not expressed in its harness-specific shape.
Putting into `given` preconditions the scenario does not require.
`then` that is not an array, or assertions using a kind outside the allowed list.
why: A uniform, minimal Given/When/Then shape lets each acceptance be executed by its harness and checked mechanically: one trigger keeps the scenario unambiguous, typed assertions keep outcomes verifiable.
evidence: Each acceptance has a `when` that declares exactly one trigger, expressed in the shape of its harness (e.g. http: method/path; unit: target; event: topic; ws/e2e: interactions).
Each acceptance has a `then` that is an array of assertions, each using a kind from the allowed list.

`given` declares only preconditions the scenario requires (the source lists the given fields as auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs; this list is not declared exhaustive, so a required precondition is not rejected merely for its field name).
verifier_detail: Term given_fields: preconditions: auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs. (Listed fields; no values.allowed declaration, so not an exclusive allow-list — the 'only' constraint concerns whether a precondition is required.)
Term assertion_kind: a then assertion kind. values.allowed = [status, body, headers, error, event_published, state_changed, metric].
Harness-specific when keys: http: method/path; unit: target; event: topic; ws/e2e: interactions.
Source example (http when): when.http: {method: POST, path: /api/users, body: {name: John}}
Source example (unit when): when.unit: {target: UserService.createUser, args: {userData: {name: John}}}
Source example (then): then: [{kind: status, expect: 200}, {kind: error, expect: {code: USER_EXISTS}}]
